title: THE FLYWHEEL
logline: A case built exhibit by exhibit from public documents: why ChatGPT, which OpenAI says more than a billion people use every week, is nearly free, how your clicks, chats and code help train the next model, who gets steamrolled when the wheel turns, and the one asset no release can upgrade for you.
director_statement: An investigative documentary with a noir pulse, never fiction. A plain-spoken narrator opens a case file on a gift a billion people accepted and builds it, exhibit by exhibit, from the companies' own public documents. Those documents are read by one archive voice whose line clears from old radio to phone to clean as the dates approach 2026, and a calm 'For the record' voice says the fair caveats aloud. Ordinary users' voices whisper requests to the machine in the dark, answer the wheel as it turns, and at dawn say 'Guard it. Train it. Move it.' to themselves. The sound is cold and tactile (tape hiss, projector, stamps, a door latch, a lone clock) over one D-minor score of felt piano, low strings and pulsing synth that tightens with each exhibit. It cuts to true silence twice: after the coders' exhibit, and on 'And part of the price is paid in data. Yours.' At the warning, the reel runs out while the wheel keeps turning, the film burns through to daylight, the falling gift motif rises in D major, and the film ends warm on 'Invest consciously.'

cast.purpose: The documentary narrator: an investigator who builds the case exhibit by exhibit from public documents, plain and factual, ending warm. Carries every claim and number (371 words, about 72%). Selection rule (DOCUMENTARY REGISTER must-fix): design 3 previews, audition each on co-gift, d-80pct, the whispered e-yours and f-final, and pick the LEAST theatrical one that stays warm and intelligible. Reject any take that sounds like a trailer announcer or a detective pastiche. Fallback: premade Bill (pqHfZKP75CvOlQylNhV4), stability 0.45, same settings.
cast.design_prompt: Male, mid-fifties, neutral General American accent. Warm, low baritone with a light natural grain and clear, precise consonants. A calm, plain-spoken documentary narrator, like an investigative journalist laying out evidence to one listener: quietly serious, measured, with natural pauses and a little warmth. Never theatrical, never a movie-trailer, announcer or detective-pastiche read, never gravelly for effect, never shouting. Can drop to a soft, clean whisper. Recorded close to a large-diaphragm microphone in an acoustically dead room: intimate and dry, with no reverb, no music and no background noise. An original voice that must not imitate any real actor, narrator or public figure.

cast.purpose: The generic document reader (Alice) for 2020-2023 company documents: the OpenAI launch post and the GPT-4 announcement (2 reads, 16 words). Reads verbatim and unemotionally, like a clerk reading into the record over an old broadcast line. THE VOICE DEVICE: one reader, filtered by the date of the document (radio for 2022-23, phone for 2025, clean for 2026), so the record gets clearer as the case nears the present. Every read is labelled on screen 'READ BY AN AI VOICE'. INTELLIGIBILITY GATE (must-fix): run ASR on every take against the exact quote text and keep only takes at or below 5% word error. If the old_radio preset loses words, drop the preset and use small_room at distance 0.3 with a 300-3400 Hz band-pass in the mix. Never paraphrase to fix intelligibility.

Same reader (Alice) for the 2025 OpenAI sycophancy postmortem (1 read, 14 words). The line is clearer now. Same ASR gate (5% WER or less). Fallback if bright_phone smears consonants: no preset, small_room, distance 0.2, gentle 250 Hz high-pass in the mix.

Same reader (Alice) for the 2026 GitHub Blog (1 read, 16 words: '...from developers like you.'). No filter, and no tape hiss under it: the record is clear now. It is the last spoken line before the hard cut to silence.

'For the record': the film's fairness conscience, a calm neutral second presence across the desk that states the hedges aloud. Exactly THREE spoken beats in the film, so it stays a device and does not become a disclaimer (40 words): a-record (not every chat), c-record (a reaction, not a count; thin wrappers versus squeezed or bought), e-record (there is a switch). Flat, precise, never sarcastic.
Cold-open chorus voice 1 of 6: generic, illustrative user, a whispered request into a phone. Labelled on screen 'ILLUSTRATIVE PROMPTS · AI VOICES · NOT REAL USERS'.
Chorus: a tired developer at a desk. Returns in Exhibit B to answer the narrator ('Perfect. Thumbs up.'), which sets up the thumbs-data document.
Chorus: a worried adult asking something private. The same voice returns, unfiltered, as ECHO_C in the finale.
Chorus: a busy person, flat and quick. Returns in Exhibit B ('Summarize this.') as the wheel's first station.
Chorus: a tender, personal request. The same voice returns, unfiltered, as ECHO_A in the finale.
Chorus: the last, closest, hesitant voice before the hard cut. The same voice returns, unfiltered, as ECHO_B in the finale.

One illustrative founder (generic premade voice, Eric) pitching on a demo-day stage, cut off mid-sentence by the narrator's warning (7 words). Played sincerely, never mocked; labelled 'ILLUSTRATIVE PITCH · AI VOICE'.

Finale echo (the payoff): the people who whispered requests to the machine now say the verbs to themselves. Same voice as VOICES_5, now without the phone filter, in a soft hall. Stacked with ECHO_B (+35 ms) and ECHO_C (+70 ms), panned -0.5 / 0 / +0.5, 9 dB under the narrator, entering about 0.3-0.5 s after the narrator's 'it'. No subtitle bar.
Finale echo: same voice as VOICES_6, unfiltered, in a hall, +35 ms after ECHO_A, centred.
Finale echo: same voice as VOICES_3, unfiltered, in a hall, +70 ms after ECHO_A, panned right.
